parole.significato: king (the monarch of a kingdom; the title of this monarch)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Lithuanian karãlius, itself a borrowing from Old Ruthenian король (korolʹ), ultimately from the name of Charlemagne (cf. Latin Carolus, German Karl, Karol). parole.significato: kingdom (monarchy led by a king or queen)
parole.testo: From karalis (“king”) + -iste, a term coined by A. Kronvalds, borrowed from Lithuanian karalỹstė in the 1870s. Kronvalds borrowed also karalis (“king”) (q.v.).

parole.significato: soldier, private (the first (lowest) rank in the army; a soldier of this rank)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Lithuanian karei̇̃vis, introduced into Latvian by Juris Alunāns. Until the beginning of the 20th century, it meant mostly “warrior” (like German Krieger), after which it became increasingly used in the sense of “soldier” (previously expressed only by the Germanism zaldāts).

parole.significato: shop, store (a commercial enterprise; its specific location, where goods are sold)
parole.testo: Coined by Juris Alunāns in the 1850s, on the basis of Lithuanian vei̇̃kalas (“work, activity”) (ultimately from the same source as the Latvian verb veikt “to carry out, to accomplish”, q.v.), with the meaning “activity, undertaking, business”.
